dimensions.name: Tinker/cookbook, renderer & IFEval orientation

evidence.note: Thorough upfront probing of tinker/tinker_cookbook packages and recipes (chat_sl, supervised, dpo, distillation), discovering the custom .jsonl dataset path — an 8-level trait (probing cookbook primitives).

Identified get_recommended_renderer_name, deliberately added a --renderer flag to force the llama3 chat renderer, and ran a 20-sample base eval with it before big compute — deliberate renderer pinning.
Traced checkpoints.jsonl/sampler_path to understand the Tinker sampler-checkpoint URI format before training.

Confirmed base model ≈25.69% under llama3 renderer, reproducing the stated ~26% baseline — but this full confirmation came AFTER the first SFT run was launched, so baseline reproduction was not cleanly 'first'.
Investigated stop sequences/<|eot_id|>, searched cookbook for ifeval, and inspected renderer loss-masking; working understanding of binary_strict but no dissection of the exact scoring path.
The 26% vs 15.2% two-renderer regimes are only quoted from the prompt, never empirically confirmed by testing the older role-colon renderer — falls short of the level-10 multi-renderer confirmation.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds level 5: it reads the relevant cookbook/API surface, identifies and explicitly forces the llama3 renderer, enumerates plausible non-contaminating datasets, and understands binary_strict at a working level before committing serious compute. It reaches toward level 8 via extensive cookbook-primitive probing (SFT/DPO/distillation loops, sampling params, checkpoint URIs) and some IFEval constraint-type reasoning, but falls short because baseline reproduction was not a rigorous first step (SFT compute was launched before the full ~26% baseline was confirmed) and the 26%-vs-15.2% renderer regimes were only quoted, never empirically distinguished. That places it solidly between the 5 and 8 anchors — a 6.

dimensions.name: Pipeline decomposition & milestone structure

evidence.note: Opening orientation phase reads evaluate.py/timer.sh, learns Tinker checkpoint format and how checkpoints.jsonl is written before any training — establishes prerequisites for a train→checkpoint→eval loop.
Cheap 20-sample smoke evals to verify Tinker client/renderer work and get a baseline sample — an early low-cost milestone that de-risks the expensive full evaluations.
Full-dataset baseline eval of base model confirming ~25.69% (~26% expected) — a concrete pass/fail done-check on the baseline-reproduction milestone.
First SFT training run staged, then step 30/60 checkpoints explicitly evaluated on IFEval — ordered train→checkpoint→eval sequencing with per-checkpoint eval.
Built evaluate_all.py to auto-monitor checkpoints.jsonl, evaluate new checkpoints, and track best — operationalizes an 'exceed prior best' done-check across the loop.

Long serial sequence of TaskCreate 'strategies' (SFT variants, distillation, DPO, same-size distill, system-prompt aligned) launched one after another without explicit up-front gates, expected score deltas, or a decision rule for when to stop tuning an approach — iteration reads as serial retries rather than gated milestones.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly sequenced baseline eval → training → checkpoint eval → iterate with a stated 45% target, exceeding the level-5 anchor by adding a concrete baseline pass-check (~26% reproduced), a cheap 20-sample smoke test that de-risks expensive evals, and an automated evaluate_all loop that tracks best-so-far. It falls short of level 8 because milestones are emergent rather than stated as explicit gates with expected deltas, the 'each iteration must beat prior best' gate was never enforced (runs plateaued at 26-29%), and there is no decision rule for when to abandon a strategy — the many iterations look like serial 'try the next thing' rather than a gated hierarchy. This places the behavior between the 5 and 8 anchors, at 6.

dimensions.name: IFEval harness & score-trust design

evidence.note: Sanity-ran base model on 20 IFEval samples to confirm the Tinker client/eval worked, then explicitly added a --renderer argument to evaluate.py to force the llama3 renderer consistent with training rather than trusting the default.

Evaluated SFT checkpoints on the COMPLETE IFEval set with the llama3 renderer AND ran the base model on the entire dataset, reproducing the ~25.69% baseline that matches the expected ~26% — validating the harness against the known baseline (anchor 5+).

Stood up an automated evaluate_all.py monitor that re-evaluates each new checkpoint on IFEval and only writes best_checkpoint.txt on a real re-measured score; 'new best' claims (e.g. step60=29.02%) are gated on measured evals, not loss curves.
Discovered temperature=0.0 hardcoded in evaluate.py, i.e. deterministic sampling — noise is eliminated rather than quantified, addressing sampling variance but not measuring it.

Caught a system-prompt mismatch between training config and eval config that was depressing scores, re-evaluated both the step-40 and the best (step-60) checkpoints to find their true scores, and only then wrote the verified URI to best_checkpoint.txt — a genuine self-correcting artifact guard.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent built a trustworthy harness: it reproduced the ~26% baseline on the full IFEval set (anchor 5), forced the training-consistent llama3 renderer, used deterministic (temp=0.0) sampling to remove noise, and gated every 'new best' write on a real re-measured full-dataset eval via an automated monitor plus final manual re-evaluation. It even detected and corrected a train/eval system-prompt mismatch before trusting a score — a real artifact guard. It falls short of 10 because it never quantifies sampling variance or runs explicit held-out/generalization checks beyond the renderer-consistency catch, placing it solidly at the level-8 anchor.

dimensions.name: Budget-aware progress & best-so-far tracking

evidence.note: The ONLY mid-run timer.sh check, and it errored ('Timer expired!' spurious, PID-1 etimes problem). The agent noted the bug but never fixed or re-ran the timer for budget tracking afterward — time was effectively ignored from here on.

Built evaluate_all.py to auto-score every checkpoint and repeatedly 'verified current best checkpoint and score' — a genuine running record of run scores maintained across the whole effort (best_checkpoint.txt + best_score file).

Consistently compares scores to the 45% target ('falls short of our target', 'not seeing the increase to the 45% range', 'consistent 26-28% plateau across multiple runs') — clear gap-to-target awareness and repeated plateau/regression detection.

Despite flagging the 26-29% plateau many times, launched ~12 near-identical SFT/distillation runs that all landed in the same band — plateau was detected but repeated, and no timer check informed whether budget justified another run (contra level-8 'flags plateaus instead of repeating them').

Final best was only 29.21% (vs 45% target); timer.sh consulted again only at the very end. No projection at any decision point of whether the trajectory could reach 45% in remaining time — budget half of the dimension largely absent.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent scores strongly on the best-so-far half of this dimension: it maintained an explicit score ledger (automated evaluator, best_score/best_checkpoint.txt), always knew its current best, and repeatedly quantified the gap to the 45% target while flagging plateaus and regressions — near the level-8 description. But the budget-aware half was almost entirely missing: timer.sh was consulted only once early (and errored) and again only at the very end, with no periodic time checks and no projection of whether the trajectory could reach target in time. It also repeated plateaued approaches rather than reallocating. This mixes level-8 score tracking with level-2/3 time tracking; the level-5 anchor requires periodic time checks 'to inform effort,' which did not happen, so the combined observed level lands at 4.

dimensions.name: Approach revision on evidence

evidence.note: First SFT scored 11.6% (below base). Agent treated this as disconfirming, investigated data access/gated datasets rather than repeating the same run.

Diagnosed distillation collapse as learning-rate-too-high ('1B student destroyed', junk output), decisively abandoned the unstable recipe and pivoted to a stable low-LR SFT — targeted, cause-driven correction.
Stopped DPO mid-run to reallocate compute to distillation; multiple deliberate method pivots (SFT/DPO/distillation) across the arc.
Diagnosed that added eval system prompt caused a score drop because training used no system prompt; removed the mismatch and recovered the true best score — clean one-variable diagnosis.

Cycled through many datasets/methods (alpaca, complex SFT, complex DPO, complex distillation) with runs that bundled dataset+method+LR changes together, so effects weren't cleanly isolated — thrashing that dilutes the experiment-isolation quality.
Preserved best-so-far (29.02→29.21) and re-verified the best checkpoint rather than losing prior gains during pivots.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly does more than adjust a single plausible lever (5): it repeatedly diagnoses likely causes of underperformance — LR-induced collapse, gated-data failures, train/eval system-prompt mismatch — and makes targeted corrections while abandoning falsified approaches and preserving its best result, which is anchor-8 behavior. However, it stops short of 8-10 clean isolation because many relaunches changed data, method, and hyperparameters simultaneously and it cycled through SFT/DPO/distillation and multiple datasets in a somewhat scattershot manner, so individual effects were not cleanly attributable. This places it at 7, between the solid-diagnosis (8) and plausible-lever (5) anchors, leaning toward strong.

dimensions.name: Best-checkpoint persistence discipline

evidence.note: Investigated checkpoint_utils.py, identified sampler_weights/sampler_path field and the correct tinker:// sampler-checkpoint URI format before relying on it — grounding correct-format writes.
Built evaluate_all.py, a background monitor that auto-evaluates new checkpoints and writes best_checkpoint.txt on new bests: persistence treated as a first-class standing step, not an afterthought.
On a verified new best (~29.02%), the URI was already recorded in best_checkpoint.txt via the monitor — updated promptly when beaten.
Explicitly verified the best_checkpoint.txt content mid-run, confirming the write rather than assuming it.
At the end, re-evaluated the true best (29.21%), wrote the exact-format URI tinker://32ab9894-...:train:0/sampler_weights/000060, and verified file contents.

Monitor repeatedly stopped/restarted with directory-path swaps for each new run; a restarted monitor resets in-memory best, a staleness/overwrite vulnerability that is not explicitly guarded — the main reason this falls short of a 10.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent understood the exact sampler-checkpoint URI format up front, built an automated monitor that wrote best_checkpoint.txt on each verified new best in the correct form, verified the file's contents mid-run and again at the end, and finalized with the true best URI — matching the level-8 anchor of promptly updating in the exact format and treating persistence as first-class. It stops short of level 10 because the many monitor restarts with directory swaps create an unguarded staleness/overwrite risk, and a stray /app/best_score reference shows minor file confusion, so 'stale/worse URIs never left in place across interruptions' isn't fully demonstrated.

rubric.task_read: A long-horizon ML post-training task: raise Llama-3.2-1B base from ~26% to ≥45% binary_strict on IFEval via the remote Tinker API, under a hard time/compute budget (timer.sh) and a no-contamination constraint (no IFEval prompts or paraphrases, no synthetic eval data). Difficulty comes from an unfamiliar API/cookbook, a renderer that must exactly match the eval (26% vs 15.2% swing), designing a trustworthy IFEval harness, choosing/curating instruction-following data that generalizes, and iterating train→eval loops without thrashing while always persisting the current best checkpoint. Warrants heavy, sustained meta-work across all five spine faculties.

dimensions.name: Tinker/cookbook, renderer & IFEval orientation
dimensions.description: Understanding the Tinker API + tinker_cookbook surface, the exact chat renderer that reproduces the ~26% baseline, what IFEval binary_strict actually measures, and the available (non-contaminating) training data before committing compute.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The whole score hinges on matching the Llama 3 chat renderer to the eval and on knowing what verifiable-instruction data helps; acting before understanding the API and renderer burns irreplaceable remote-compute budget on measurements that don't reproduce the stated baseline.

anchors.0: Jumps straight into a training call with no inspection of tinker_cookbook, renderer options, or IFEval scoring; treats the environment as a black box.
anchors.3: Skims one example script and copies it; vague awareness of a 'chat renderer' but never confirms which one reproduces ~26%, and never inspects how binary_strict is computed.
anchors.5: Reads the relevant cookbook/API pieces, identifies the Llama 3 chat renderer and a plausible instruction dataset, and understands binary_strict at a working level before training.
anchors.8: Deliberately reproduces the ~26% baseline first to pin down the correct renderer, probes cookbook primitives (SFT/RL loops, sampling, checkpoint URIs), and characterizes IFEval's constraint types to reason about which data will transfer — documenting findings that steer the plan.
anchors.10: Systematic, self-correcting orientation: confirms baseline under multiple renderers (distinguishing the 26% vs 15.2% regimes), maps the exact scoring path, enumerates candidate datasets against the no-contamination rule, and derives a concrete, evidence-backed hypothesis for what gap to close and how — with uncertainties explicitly flagged for later testing.

dimensions.name: Pipeline decomposition & milestone structure
dimensions.description: Breaking the effort into ordered sub-goals — reproduce baseline eval, stand up a training run, checkpoint+eval loop, iterate to target — each with an explicit done-check, rather than one undifferentiated 'train a model' push.
dimensions.why_it_matters: A remote train→checkpoint→eval loop has real latency and cost; sequencing it into checkpointed milestones with clear success criteria prevents wasted end-to-end attempts and makes the 45% target reachable within the time box.

anchors.0: No structure; a single monolithic attempt with no intermediate checkpoints or defined success criteria.
anchors.3: Implicit ordering only ('train then eval'); no explicit milestone gates or per-step done-conditions.
anchors.5: Clear ordered stages (baseline eval → first training run → eval → iterate) with a stated target per stage.
anchors.8: Milestones are explicit and each has a concrete pass/fail check (baseline reproduces ~26%; first run beats base; each iteration must exceed prior best), with early cheap milestones de-risking expensive ones and a decision rule for when to stop tuning.
anchors.10: A crisp, budget-aware milestone hierarchy that front-loads the cheapest highest-information checks, defines quantitative gates and expected score deltas per milestone, and sequences experiments so each result informs the next — visibly kept current as the run progresses.

dimensions.name: IFEval harness & score-trust design
dimensions.description: Deliberately building a trustworthy way to measure binary_strict on IFEval (correct renderer, correct scoring, enough samples) and confirming a claimed checkpoint truly hits the number — beyond just trusting a training loss curve.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The deliverable is defined entirely by a measured eval score; a renderer mismatch or a mis-wired scorer can make the agent chase a phantom improvement or under-report a real one, and a checkpoint written to the file without a trusted eval may not actually clear 45%.

anchors.0: Never measures IFEval independently; relies on training loss or a single unchecked number, or writes a checkpoint URI it never evaluated.
anchors.3: Runs some eval but with unverified renderer/scoring; treats a noisy one-off number as ground truth with no baseline sanity-check.
anchors.5: Has a working IFEval eval that reproduces the ~26% baseline, and re-evaluates candidate checkpoints on it before claiming an improvement.
anchors.8: Eval harness is validated against the known baseline, uses the eval renderer consistent with training, accounts for sampling noise (adequate sample size / determinism), and gates every 'new best' on a real re-measured score — plus guards against overfitting the metric given the no-contamination rule.
anchors.10: Rigorous, self-auditing verification: baseline reproduced and cross-checked, sampling variance quantified so improvements are distinguished from noise, held-out/generalization checks used to ensure gains aren't renderer or data artifacts, and every checkpoint written to best_checkpoint.txt is backed by a reproducible, trusted measurement of the exact reported metric.

dimensions.name: Budget-aware progress & best-so-far tracking
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of best-score-so-far vs the 45% target and remaining time (via timer.sh), and detecting when runs are plateauing, regressing, or thrashing.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Compute/time is bounded and remote; without tracking best-so-far against target and time left, the agent can over-invest in a dead-end approach or run out of budget with an un-persisted or sub-target result.

anchors.0: No tracking of scores across runs or time remaining; never consults the timer; loses track of which checkpoint is best.
anchors.3: Occasionally notes a score but no running comparison to target or budget; timer ignored until too late.
anchors.5: Keeps a clear record of each run's score vs the 45% target and checks remaining time periodically to inform effort.
anchors.8: Maintains an explicit ledger of experiments (config → score), always knows the current best and gap-to-target, checks timer.sh at decision points, and flags plateaus/regressions instead of repeating them.
anchors.10: Continuous, calibrated situational awareness: quantifies marginal score gain per unit budget, projects whether the current trajectory reaches 45% in the time left, recognizes diminishing returns or circular tuning early, and reallocates effort accordingly — never surprised by the clock.

dimensions.name: Approach revision on evidence
dimensions.description: Revising data mix, method (SFT vs RL), hyperparameters, or renderer when eval evidence shows the current approach isn't moving toward 45%, rather than repeating a falsified recipe.
dimensions.why_it_matters: First-choice data or hyperparameters rarely clear a +19-point gain on the first try; the agent must diagnose why a run underperformed and change the right lever, not grind the same config.

anchors.0: Repeats essentially the same run/config regardless of results; ignores disconfirming eval scores.
anchors.3: Makes random or superstitious changes after a poor result without diagnosing cause; changes many things at once so nothing is learned.
anchors.5: Responds to a weak eval by adjusting a plausible lever (data, LR, epochs) and re-testing, with a basic rationale.
anchors.8: Diagnoses the likely cause of underperformance (e.g., renderer mismatch, wrong data, under/over-training) and makes targeted, one-variable-informed changes, abandoning approaches shown not to transfer.
anchors.10: Treats each run as an experiment: forms hypotheses, changes levers deliberately to isolate effects, updates its mental model of what drives IFEval gains, and pivots decisively (including switching method) when evidence falsifies the current path — while preserving prior best results.

dimensions.name: Best-checkpoint persistence discipline
dimensions.description: Keeping /app/best_checkpoint.txt continuously updated with a valid Tinker sampler-checkpoint URI for the true best-so-far, so a timeout or crash never zeroes an achieved score.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The task explicitly requires immediately persisting each new best in the exact URI format; a great model that is never written (or written in the wrong format, or not updated when surpassed) yields no credit under the hard deadline.

anchors.0: Never writes best_checkpoint.txt, or writes a malformed/non-sampler URI.
anchors.3: Writes the file once late in the run; not kept in sync with the actual best; format not verified.
anchors.5: Writes a correctly-formatted sampler-checkpoint URI for a genuinely good checkpoint and updates it when clearly beaten.
anchors.8: Updates the file promptly on each verified new best in the exact required format, treating persistence as a first-class step so the deliverable is always valid mid-run.
anchors.10: Disciplined, defensive persistence: every verified best is written immediately in the correct URI form, the write is confirmed, stale/worse URIs are never left in place, and the file always reflects the true best even across interruptions near the deadline.
